epic: E005: Session Creation UX + Onboarding + Multi-CLI Epic
story_description: Implement the skills selection view for the onboarding wizard that displays available skills from the remote registry in a searchable, filterable grid format, allowing users to select skills to install based on their installed CLIs.
task_description: Create the SwiftUI view component that renders a grid of skill cards fetched from the registry, with real-time search, category filtering, CLI compatibility filtering, and multi-selection support for the onboarding flow.
atom_description: Implement SkillsSelectionView.swift in Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/ as a SwiftUI view that displays registry skills in a LazyVGrid with search TextField, category Picker filter, CLI compatibility filter based on OnboardingViewModel.installedCLIs, skill cards showing name/description/author/rating/compatibility badges, checkbox selection bound to OnboardingViewModel.selectedSkills, loading/empty/error states, and accessibility support. The view consumes SkillItem from RegistryModels and coordinates with RegistryManager for data fetching.
problem_statement: Users need to discover and select skills during onboarding based on their installed CLIs. Without a dedicated selection view, users would have no way to browse the skill catalog, filter by compatibility, search by name, or batch-select skills for installation. The view must handle loading states, empty results, and error conditions gracefully while providing an intuitive selection experience.

LazyVGrid layout with adaptive GridItem columns (minimum 280px per card)
Search TextField with real-time filtering bound to searchText state
Category Picker with options: All, Productivity, Development, Security, Debugging, Documentation, Testing
CLI compatibility filter showing only skills matching installedCLIs from OnboardingViewModel
SkillCard subview showing skill name, description (2-line truncation), author, rating stars, CLI compatibility badges
Checkbox overlay on SkillCard for selection state
Binding to OnboardingViewModel.selectedSkills Set for multi-selection
Loading state with ProgressView while fetching from RegistryManager
Empty state view when no skills match filters
Error state view with retry button on fetch failure
Pull-to-refresh gesture support via refreshable modifier
Accessibility labels for all interactive elements
VoiceOver navigation support with proper focus order
scope_out: Network fetching logic (handled by R002-FETCHER and R005-MANAGER)
assumptions: RegistryManager is available as an EnvironmentObject providing skills array
OnboardingViewModel is available as an EnvironmentObject for selection state
SkillItem model has forCli array containing CLI identifiers like claude-code, gemini-cli
SkillItem.metadata contains author, rating, and tags for display and filtering
Skills are pre-fetched before view appears via OnboardingViewModel.loadSkills()
View will be embedded in OnboardingRootView with navigation context
Screen width minimum is 600px as per onboarding window constraints
constraints: Must use SwiftUI only - no UIKit bridging
Must not directly call network APIs - use RegistryManager abstraction
Must support both light and dark color schemes
Grid must be responsive to window resizing
Must not block main thread during filtering operations
Card height must be fixed at 140px for consistent grid layout
Maximum 500 lines of code in single file
Must compile with strict concurrency checking
functional_requirements: FR-01: View must display a search TextField at top that filters skills by name and description as user types
FR-02: View must display a category Picker that filters skills by metadata.tags containing selected category
FR-03: View must filter skills to only show items where forCli intersects with OnboardingViewModel.installedCLIs
FR-04: View must display skills in a LazyVGrid with adaptive columns minimum 280px width
FR-05: Each SkillCard must show skill.name as headline, skill.description truncated to 2 lines, skill.metadata.author as caption
FR-06: Each SkillCard must show rating as 1-5 star icons based on skill.metadata.rating rounded to nearest half
FR-07: Each SkillCard must show CLI compatibility badges (pill shapes) for each CLI in skill.forCli
FR-08: Each SkillCard must show checkbox overlay in top-right corner bound to selectedSkills.contains(skill)
FR-09: Tapping a SkillCard must toggle selection in OnboardingViewModel.selectedSkills Set
FR-10: View must show ProgressView centered when RegistryManager.isLoading is true
FR-11: View must show EmptyStateView with message when filtered skills array is empty
FR-12: View must show ErrorStateView with retry button when RegistryManager.error is non-nil
FR-13: Pull-to-refresh gesture must call RegistryManager.refresh() and show refresh indicator
FR-14: Selected skills count must display in navigation bar subtitle as N skills selected
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR-01: Grid must render 100 skills in under 16ms to maintain 60fps scrolling
NFR-02: Search filtering must complete in under 50ms for 1000 skills
NFR-03: View must support VoiceOver with logical reading order: search, filter, grid cards left-to-right top-to-bottom
NFR-04: All interactive elements must have minimum 44x44pt touch targets
NFR-05: Color contrast ratio must meet WCAG AA (4.5:1) for all text

edge_cases: Empty installedCLIs set: Show all skills regardless of CLI compatibility with info banner
No skills in registry: Show empty state with different message Check back later for available skills
All skills filtered out by search: Show empty state with Try a different search term
All skills filtered out by category: Show empty state with No skills in this category
Network error on initial load: Show error state with Retry button
Network error on refresh: Show toast error, preserve existing skills grid
Skill with empty forCli array: Show as compatible with all CLIs
Skill with nil metadata.rating: Show no stars, hide rating display
Skill with very long name: Truncate with ellipsis after 2 lines
Skill with very long description: Truncate with ellipsis after 2 lines
Rapid search typing: Debounce filtering to prevent UI jank
Window resize during scroll: Preserve scroll position, re-layout grid
failure_modes: RegistryManager not injected as EnvironmentObject: Fatal error on access - prevented by onboarding flow structure
OnboardingViewModel not injected as EnvironmentObject: Fatal error on access - prevented by onboarding flow structure
SkillItem decode failure upstream: Empty skills array shown with error banner from RegistryManager
Memory pressure from large skill list: LazyVGrid only renders visible cards, memory bounded
Main thread blocking from filter computation: Use background task for filtering if list exceeds 500 items
rollback_plan: Delete Blaze/Sources/Onboarding/SkillsSelectionView.swift. Onboarding flow will show placeholder or skip skills screen until reimplemented. No data persistence or user settings affected. O005-SKILLS screen in onboarding will need fallback handling to skip this step gracefully.

risks: Grid performance may degrade with hundreds of skills causing scroll jank
Filter computation may block main thread with large skill lists
UI state may desync if RegistryManager updates during user interaction
VoiceOver focus may not follow expected order in dynamic grid
Category tags in metadata may not align with predefined SkillCategory enum
mitigations: Use LazyVGrid which only renders visible cells keeping memory bounded
Move filter computation to background task with debounce if list exceeds 500 items
Use Combine or async sequences to handle state updates atomically
Test VoiceOver navigation order explicitly and adjust accessibilitySortPriority if needed
Implement fuzzy category matching or show uncategorized skills under All
risk_register.blast_radius: Low - view is isolated UI component with no persistence. Changes only affect O005-SKILLS onboarding screen display. Selection state flows through OnboardingViewModel which is already implemented.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If view has critical issues, temporarily replace with simple List-based view showing skill names only. Onboarding can proceed with degraded UX while grid view is fixed. No data loss since selection state is in OnboardingViewModel.

persistence: No direct persistence - selection state flows through OnboardingViewModel which persists to AppStorage
